findings.title: Italian text placed in the Lithuanian login translation
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The PR was supposed to strip the `<a>` links from this key because the English source (`messages_en.properties` `loginTotpStep1`) contains no HTML, but instead the Italian translation was pasted in. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions for setting up their authenticator. Should read a Lithuanian sentence equivalent to 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

findings.title: Italian text placed in the Lithuanian account translation
findings.body: `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian in the Lithuanian account message bundle (the same mistake as the login bundle). The other locales in this PR (fi, sv, sk) received properly translated text; the Lithuanian one appears to have been copied from the Italian bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian text for the TOTP setup step.

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat in an i18next bundle
findings.body: This account-console bundle uses i18next `{{...}}` interpolation for numeric arguments throughout (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' ... {{1}}.`). This PR changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` from `... {{0}} ... {{1}} ... {{2}} value(s).` to `... {0} ... {1} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` — single braces plus a Java `ChoiceFormat` expression. i18next does not understand either form, so when this key is rendered it will show the raw placeholders (including the literal `{2,choice,0#values|...}`) instead of an interpolated message. The same incorrect change is applied in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` (~line 3139). Those client bundles should keep the `{{...}}` style; the `choice` format belongs only in the Java theme bundles.

findings.title: Message bundles read as ISO-8859-1 while files are UTF-8
findings.body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))` decodes the properties using ISO-8859-1, but Keycloak message files are UTF-8 (they contain raw CJK/Arabic/etc. characters, e.g. `messages_zh_CN.properties` `doLogIn=登录`). This differs from `verify()` which reads the file with `Files.readString` (UTF-8). Tag detection still works because tags are ASCII bytes, but every non-ASCII value is decoded to mojibake; consequently the diagnostic strings produced from `value.substring(...)` (and any non-ASCII-dependent logic) will be corrupted, and the two code paths disagree about the file content. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese characters in a zh_CN (Simplified) bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the Simplified-Chinese (zh_CN) resource. Mainland Simplified wording would be `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`. As written the locale shows the wrong script to Simplified-Chinese users.

findings.title: No positive test that legitimate/matching HTML produces no messages
findings.body:
All added tests assert that something is flagged (`Illegal HTML` or `Didn't find anchor tag`) or that duplicate keys are detected. There is no test asserting that a translation which faithfully reproduces the English HTML — matching `` anchors, allowed `/

//
` — yields an empty message list. Because the check compares the sanitizer's normalized output against the raw value, false positives from benign normalization (e.g. `
` vs `
`, attribute quoting, uppercase tags) are the main failure mode, and with no positive/negative test a regression that starts rejecting valid translations would go unnoticed by the unit suite.
